sections.label: Minimum tax for multinationals
sections.summary: The rules require large multinational enterprises to pay a minimum effective tax rate of 15% wherever they operate.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The rules require large multinational enterprises to pay a minimum effective tax rate of 15%, wherever they operate.

sections.label: Top-up taxes start date
sections.summary: Both top-up taxes apply to businesses' financial years commencing on or after 1 January 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Both top-up taxes apply to businesses' financial years commencing on or after 1 January 2025.

sections.label: Deduction for green certificates
sections.summary: Clause 19 provides a 100% tax deduction for expenses incurred by businesses on green certificates or credits.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Clause 19 provides for a 100% tax deduction for expenses incurred by businesses on green certificates or credits.

sections.label: Personal income tax rebate
sections.summary: Clause 55 provides all tax-resident individuals a 60% Personal Income Tax Rebate for Year of Assessment 2025, capped at $200 per taxpayer.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow) (for the Second Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Clause 55 provides for all tax-resident individuals to receive a Personal Income Tax Rebate of 60% for the Year of Assessment 2025, capped at $200 per taxpayer.

sections.label: Budget 2025 tax rebates
sections.summary: The Bill delivers Budget 2025's intent, providing a 60% personal income tax rebate capped at $200 and a 50% corporate tax rebate capped at $40,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This Bill delivers on the intent of Budget 2025: to strengthen fiscal sustainability while easing cost pressures on Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It provides immediate relief through a 60%personal income tax rebate, capped at $200; and a 50% corporate tax rebate, capped at $40,000, to help both households and firms manage near-term costs.

sections.label: Training scheme tax exemption
sections.summary: Allowances under the Workfare Training Support Scheme, SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme and Workfare Skills Support (Level-Up) Scheme are tax exempt, with refunds requiring application to IRAS before 31 December 2029.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Another welcome change is the tax exemption for allowances under the Workfare Training Support Scheme, the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme and the Workfare Skills Support (Level-Up) Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This rightly ensures that training and upskilling benefits are not taxed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: However, I note that individuals who previously paid tax on these payments must apply to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) for refunds before 31 December 2029.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry consider an automatic refund instead, and share how many individuals and how much tax collected, since 2013, will be affected by this retrospective exemption?

sections.label: Personal income tax rebate 2025
sections.summary: Clause 55 grants a personal income tax rebate of 60% of tax payable, capped at $200, for YA 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Under clause 55 of the Bill, a personal income tax rebate worth 60% of tax payable, capped at $200, will be granted for the Year of Assessment (YA) 2025.

sections.label: Tax bracket update and rebate cap
sections.summary: The speaker notes tax brackets were last updated in 2001 and estimates close to 80% of resident taxpayers receive only the $200 cap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: After all, the last time the personal income tax brackets were last updated was more than 24 years ago in 2001.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Based on my estimates, close to 80% of resident taxpayers will only receive the $200 cap, which means that the headline 60% rebate appears more generous than it really is.

sections.label: Corporate income tax rebate clause
sections.summary: Clause 43 introduces a new section 92L providing for a 50% corporate income tax rebate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Turning to clause 43, which introduces a new section 92L, providing for a 50% corporate income tax rebate.

sections.label: Restructured relief for children
sections.summary: The relief was restructured for children born on or after January 2024 to fixed amounts of $8,000, $10,000 and $12,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As I have shared previously, this relief was restructured for children born on or after January 2024 from a percentage-based formula to a fixed dollar amount of $8,000 for the first child, $10,000 for the second and $12,000 for the third and subsequent children.

sections.label: Family office capital deployment rules
sections.summary: Family offices must invest the lower of 10% of AUM or $10 million, and the speaker urges raising this requirement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Under current rules, family offices must invest the lower of 10% of AUM or $10 million in designated investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This means that the actual capital deployed into Singapore's productive economy may be far smaller than the headline numbers intended.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I would urge the Government to strengthen this capital deployment requirement, perhaps, by raising it to at least 15% to 20% of AUM and/or tightening the definition of eligible investments to require a minimum portion in Singapore listed equities, Real Estate Investment Trust (REITS) or funds with domestic exposure even as I note that there is a 1.5 to two times multiplier applied to certain investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, we should move away from recurring one-off measures towards structural reforms, indexing tax brackets and reliefs to inflation, updating outdated reliefs, like the Earned Income Relief, and embedding greater progressivity into our corporate tax regime.

sections.label: Global minimum tax adaptation
sections.summary: The Domestic Top-up Tax and Multinational Enterprise Top-up Tax were implemented from January 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I will focus only on the segment of the Bill that pertains to how Singapore is preparing to adapt to global minimum tax rules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We have already implemented the Domestic Top-up Tax and the Multinational Enterprise Top-up Tax from January 2025.

sections.label: Global minimum tax rules
sections.summary: The global minimum tax rules have started to make Singapore's tax incentives almost useless.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The global minimum tax rules have started to render our tax incentives almost useless.

sections.label: Income Tax Act amendments
sections.summary: The Bill amends the Income Tax Act to facilitate RIC's implementation, which the speaker fully supports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The Bill makes amendments to the Income Tax Act to facilitate RIC's implementation and I fully support it.

sections.label: Uncertain fiscal outlook response
sections.summary: They said the impact on the fiscal outlook was uncertain and they were monitoring and would review their approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In their own words, they could only say that the impact on our fiscal outlook was uncertain and that they were monitoring the issue closely and would review their approach once there is greater clarity.

sections.label: Systematic surplus-sharing structures
sections.summary: The speaker agrees with Mr Louis Chua on having structures that share surpluses systematically, unlike previous ad hoc initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: To that end, in some circumstances, I also agree with Mr Louis Chua that we should have some structures that do it systematically.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: There have been previous instances of such surplus-sharing initiatives, but they have been only on an ad hoc basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Just imagine a system where if Singapore's economy does well and our tax collections are more buoyant than expected, Singaporeans will all be assured beforehand that they will benefit directly from our country's economic success.

sections.label: SGX listing tax rebate
sections.summary: Companies listing ordinary shares on the SGX between 19 February 2025 and 31 December 2027 receive a five-year tax rebate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Companies that list their ordinary shares on the SGX between 19 February 2025 and 31 December 2027, new listings or re-listings, both primary and secondary listings, will qualify.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The company receives a tax rebate for five years, 20% corporate tax for periods of a primary listing; and 10% for a secondary listing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These are capped at $6 million a year, if the market cap is at or above $1 billion on listing date; and $3 million a year if below that figure.

sections.label: FY2025 SGX new listings
sections.summary: In Financial Year 2025, SGX had six new listings, raising $25.7 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In Financial Year (FY) 2025, SGX had six new listings, raising $25.7 million.

sections.label: Time-limited measures until 2027
sections.summary: These measures are time-limited until the end of 2027.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Last, and most importantly, these measures are time-limited until the end of 2027.

sections.label: Removal of SGX financial watchlist
sections.summary: SGX RegCo announced on 29 October it would remove the financial watchlist and introduce more flexible listing rules under a disclosure-based approach, which the speaker disagrees with.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On 29 October, SGX RegCo announced it would remove the financial watchlist and introduce more flexible listing rules under a "disclosure-based approach." This is a bit paradoxical to me.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What SGX calls a more "disclosure-based approach" can actually mean more disclosure for poor companies while keeping them listed and trading, but less actionable disclosure and actionable information for the market as a whole.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I therefore disagree with the removal of the watchlist.

sections.label: Taiwan versus Singapore retail participation
sections.summary: Taiwan's 54% retail participation versus Singapore's 21% shows what happens when retail investors have confidence built on quality signals like watchlists and Investor Protection Centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Taiwan's 54% retail participation versus our 21% shows what happens when retail investors have confidence – confidence built on quality signals like watchlists and Investor Protection Centres.

sections.label: STI sector allocation breakdown
sections.summary: The STI comprises Financials at 54%, REITs at 16.4%, Industrials at 9.8%, Telecom at 7.5% and Utilities at 4.9%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Big allocators need clarity about what each allocation represents in their portfolio.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But look at the STI: Financials – 54%, Real Estate Investment Trusts or REITS – 16.4%, Industrials – 9.8%, Telecom – 7.5%, Utilities – 4.9%.

sections.label: SGX support for growing SMEs
sections.summary: SGX should look out for growing SMEs and cultivate a listing pipeline, including replacing the sponsor-based Catalist board with a non-trading incubation board that graduates to OTC-style boards before mainboard listing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: SGX should become an exchange that looks out for growing SMEs and cultivates a pipeline for listing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This should include overhauling the sponsor-based Catalist board, to be replaced by a non-trading, capacity-building "incubation board" which graduates to OTC-style boards as a prelude to mainboard listing.

sections.label: Tessa Therapeutics collapse illustration
sections.summary: The 2023 collapse of Tessa Therapeutics, despite raising over US$200 million, illustrates the brittleness of relying solely on late stage venture funding without domestic capital market support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The collapse of Tessa Therapeutics in 2023, despite raising over US$200 million, illustrates the brittleness of relying solely on late stage venture funding without domestic capital market support.

sections.label: GIC investment mandate question
sections.summary: A 2 July 2024 Parliamentary Question asked whether the Government will review GIC's investment mandates to consider allocating part of its investments to Singapore Exchange-listed securities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: He did not suggest what the Minister has called "pump-priming".

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But I did manage to find this exchange while digging in the Hansard, a Parliamentary Question from 2 July 2024, "Asked the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance whether the Government will review its investment mandates with GIC to consider the suggestion from some industry players for GIC to allocate part of its investments to securities listed on the Singapore Exchange to revitalise our local stock exchange." The source of that "pump-priming" question was Member of Parliament Liang Eng Hwa, who is not a WP Member of Parliament.

sections.label: GloBE reporting for associated entities
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry will impose GloBE reporting obligations for associated entities, often off-balance sheet, and notes Clause 45 deals with RICs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry confirm that it will impose GloBe reporting obligations for such associated entities, which are often off-balance sheet as well?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Clause 45 of the Bill deals with RICs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I had, in the debate on last year's Budget Statement, raised my concern that RICs could potentially be used as a strategic loophole by MNEs to shield themselves from their tax liabilities, specifically through recording all innovation activities in a subsidiary located in a jurisdiction with generous R&D credits.

sections.label: Pillar Two rules in force
sections.summary: More than 50 countries already have Pillar Two rules in force, and the Bill's passage consolidates Singapore's position within this group.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To date, more than 50 countries already have Pillar Two rules in force and the passage of this Bill will further consolidate our nation's own position within this group of like-minded economies.

sections.label: US terrorist stick and UTPR
sections.summary: The passage says the US has wielded the terrorist stick under the Trump administration in violation of WTO rules, making tit-for-tat threats less credible, and notes Singapore has not adopted the UTPR.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But given how US has already chosen to proactively wield the terrorist stick under the Trump administration in violation of World Trade Organization rules, the threat of such a tit-for-tat response becomes much less credible.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: That said, I note that we have yet to adopt certain elements of Pillar Two, such as the Under-Taxed Payments Rule (UTPR), in Singapore.

sections.label: Side-by-side regime for American groups
sections.summary: One possibility mentioned is a side-by-side regime giving American-owned groups exceptional treatment, including recognition of idiosyncratic MNE minimum taxes such as GILTI.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: One possibility is, as mentioned by others in this House, a side-by-side regime where American-owned groups receive some form of exceptional treatment vis-a-vis the rest of the world.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This could entail, for instance, the recognition of idiosyncratic MNE minimum taxes, such as the Global Intangible Low-Taxed Income (GILTI) for controlled foreign corporations, such that they are consistent with those prescribed by globe rules.

sections.label: GILTI not mentioned in legislation
sections.summary: The passage states there is no mention of how GILTI will be addressed in the present legislation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Similarly, there is no mention of how GILTI will be addressed in the present legislation.

sections.label: Global minimum corporate tax plan
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Ministry sees a likely scenario for the global minimum corporate tax regime and has a tentative plan to revise legislation; the Bill amends the Income Tax Act 1947 for Budget 2025 measures.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To that end, I hope that the Ministry will share whether, in its view, there is a more plausible or likely scenario among the various possibilities for how the global minimum corporate tax regime will play out and if it has sketched out a tentative plan for how we might revise the legislation as these different potential outcomes unfold.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Bill proposes amendments to the Income Tax Act 1947 and effects the measures announced in Budget 2025.

sections.label: Group-basis shareholding rule clarity
sections.summary: Under the new group-basis rule, the divesting company and its group members must collectively hold at least 20% of the investee for 24 months before disposal to qualify.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Investors welcome clarity where under the new group-basis rule, the divesting company and its group members must collectively hold at least 20% of the investee for 24 months before disposal in order to qualify.

sections.label: Pillar Two global minimum tax
sections.summary: Pillar Two backstops BEPS 2.0 by setting a global minimum tax rate of 15% to curb tax avoidance and tax competition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Pillar Two backstops the original BEPS 2.0, which acts as a global minimum tax rate, which sets a global minimum tax rate of 15% to curb tax avoidance and a senseless race to the bottom-style tax competition.

sections.label: US GILTI and Singapore top-up tax
sections.summary: The speaker seeks clarification on how Singapore's domestic top-up tax under the Multinational Enterprise (Minimum Tax) Act interacts with US GILTI and what safeguards prevent overlapping taxation of US MNEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: My concern is to ensure that Singapore remains attractive as a business hub via excellent infrastructure, a skilled workforce and political stability, notwithstanding the US decision not to fully not to fully implement the OECD Pillar Two global tax framework affects Singapore's relative competitiveness as a regional hub, particularly for US multinational corporations, headquartered and operating in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Therefore, I seek clarification of how the implementation of Singapore's domestic top-up tax under Multinational Enterprise (Minimum Tax) Act will interact with the US' GILTI and what safeguards are in place to prevent overlapping or duplicative taxation of US MNEs operating in Singapore?

sections.label: Top-up tax revenue cession
sections.summary: If a multinational enterprise is taxed below 15% in a jurisdiction, other jurisdictions may impose top-up tax, so not implementing Pillar Two taxes cedes tax revenue to other jurisdictions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: When a multinational enterprise is taxed below the minimum effective rate of 15% in a jurisdiction, other jurisdictions will have the right to impose a top-up tax on the multinational enterprise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: This design ensures that the multinational enterprises pay a minimum effective tax rate of 15% wherever they operate, even if some jurisdictions choose not to implement the rules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: Therefore, if we do not implement the Pillar Two taxes, we will cede tax revenue to other jurisdictions as the affected multinational enterprises would have to pay these taxes to other jurisdictions that have implemented Pillar Two rules.

sections.label: Related party arm's length expenditures
sections.summary: RIC recipients must ensure qualifying expenditures from transactions with related parties are at arm's length.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: The answer is, yes, the RIC recipients must ensure that qualifying expenditures incurred from transactions with related parties are at arm's length.

sections.label: Economic Strategy Review Committee
sections.summary: The Economic Strategy Review Committee was established in August to refresh Singapore's economic blueprint amid tougher competition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: But at the same time, we are under no illusions to the fact that we have to compete harder in this new world where the rules matter less and strategic heft matters more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: This is why we established the Economic Strategy Review Committee in August to refresh our economic blueprint.

sections.label: Securitisation entities tax liability
sections.summary: Securitisation entities will not be liable for unpaid tax of the multinational enterprise or appointed as filing entity unless the only constituent entity here.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: To ensure that securitisation transactions remain viable in Singapore, securitisation entities will not be liable for unpaid tax liability of the multinational enterprise or appointed as a filing entity unless it is the only constituent entity here, MOF and IRAS will also work closely with businesses and industry associations to address other remaining areas of concern and to further ease the compliance burden for businesses.

sections.label: Singapore tax information exchanges 2028
sections.summary: IRAS announced Singapore expects to commence these exchanges in 2028 and will provide further guidance to the industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: IRAS has announced that Singapore expects to commence these exchanges in 2028 and has been in close consultation with the industry since last year, and it will provide further guidance to the industry in due course.

sections.label: SG60 personal income tax rebate
sections.summary: The SG60 package includes a 60% personal income tax rebate to all tax resident individuals, estimated to cost almost $400 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: The SG60 package this year includes a 60% personal income tax rebate to all tax resident individuals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
sentences.text: This rebate is estimated to cost almost $400 million.
